purpose: Draws the Stakeholder line and the Authority line of a Plan card, and on a Development Resource the Resource Owner line: linked people and organizations as chips with their role marks, names that are not records yet as text, the picker to link a record, creating a new stakeholder, removing, and an Authority's "acts for", with every read and write supplied by the host.
namedChanges: Imports (lines 5-59): `OrgRecordPicker`, `PickerFind`, `PickerIncomplete` from `record-picker`; `FieldRow` from `field-row`; `RemoveControl` from `remove-control`; `EntityRefValue` from `entity-ref-value`; `entityRefFromFact` from `entity-ref`; `alreadyLinked`, `authoritiesOf`, `actsForOnRelation`, `RESOURCE_OWNER_RELATION_TYPE`, `resourceOwnersOf`, `legacyAuthorityOf`, `sameRecord`, `stakeholdersOf`, `STAKEHOLDER_RELATION_FACT`, `STAKEHOLDER_RELATION_TYPE`, `STAKEHOLDER_ROLES`, `stakeholderTagTexts`, `stakeholdersWithoutTag`, `LinkedStakeholder`, `CONSTRAINT_AUTHORITY_WHY`, `CONSTRAINT_LAST_PERSON`, `NOT_A_PERSON`, `isPersonStakeholderType`, `removingLastPersonAuthority` from `plan-stakeholders-model`; `isResourceType` from `plan-kinds`; `rowServedFact`, `sameServedList` from `plan-card-facts`; `RecordRelation` from `relation-role`; `BaseRecord`, `GridRecord` from `base-record`. Each was compared with the source's own, comments stripped: `planStakeholders.ts` (minus the writers and finders, which are host members), `planConstraint.ts`, `planKinds.ts`, `rowServedFact`, `sameServedList` are the same; `entityRefFromFact` is the same but for guards against an undefined array element.

`@tanstack/react-query` is gone: each `useQuery` and `qc.*` call is a host member (see above), and `useQueryClient()` is not called (the query client stays in the host). `useShell()` is gone the same way. `hasSubstitutedType` (`records.ts:357`) and `memberEntityUri` (`relationWrite.ts:99`) are host members too, not copies: the first compares with the app's type namespace and the second falls back to the app's base origin, both from its configuration.

Each host call is made with the same arguments, in the same place and order as the source's call. `useHeldVaults` (lines 174-177) is `host.useHeldVaults()`; `useOpenInItsVault` takes `host.useOpenRecordInVault()` where it read `useShell()`; the line `const key = relationsKey(...)` in `remember` is gone (the host forms the key from `setRelations`' arguments); `stakeholderIncomplete` takes the host where it took the query client; `Awaited<ReturnType<typeof readRecord>>` is `Awaited<ReturnType<StakeholderLinesHost["readRecord"]>>`; the `<ConnectedCreateDialog ... />` element is a call `host.renderCreateStakeholder!({ ... })` with the same props as one object; the writers are called with a `!` after the member.
Each component reads `host` from the new `StakeholderLinesHostContext` (`useStakeholderLinesHost`, private) first; with no provider it throws.
One added line in each component, before `showPicker`: `if (!(<its writers>)) { editing = false; offer = false; }`. That is the read-only behaviour: the same as `editing` false with no `offer`.

One comment in `useLoadedStakeholder` is reworded; other comments are the source's. The app's `useMainTag(uri)` there (imported from `recordTags`) is the host member `host.useMainTag(uri)`; the `handleFromFacts` import and the `served` read are gone (the app removed them). `ConnectedCreateDialog`, `useConstraintPeople`, `ShellContext` and the app's query-key helpers are not in the unit.
